newsitem.title: USA: EMI completes restructuring in N. America.
newsitem.headline: EMI completes restructuring in N. America.

text.p: British music company EMI Group Plc said on Friday it had completed the restructuring of its North American operations.

As a consequence of business consolidation called for under the plan, the company said, 140 people will be leaving EMI, including Davitt Sigerson, pesident and chief executive of EMI Records in the United States.

EMI, whose artists include the Spice Girls, announced the restructuring in late May. The plan called for the company to take a provision of 117.2 million pounds to cover costs in streamlining its North American recorded music business.
EMI said Virgin Records and Capital Records will now be the company's principal U.S. record labels.
